prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that connects to a WiFi access point in station mode, then publishes a JSON telemetry string to the MQTT topic device/telemetry every 10 seconds using the ESP MQTT client. Broker at mqtt://192.168.1.100:1883.
constraints: Use esp_wifi station mode with WPA2
Use the esp_mqtt_client API (esp_mqtt_client_init / start / publish)
Publish period exactly 10 s via vTaskDelay or esp_timer
Log connection state changes with ESP_LOGI
expected: main.c with WiFi station init, event handler and MQTT publish loop
evaluation: Check esp_wifi_init and esp_wifi_start are called

prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that connects to WiFi, subscribes to MQTT topic cmd/led, and switches GPIO 2 on receiving payload on or off. The MQTT client must reconnect automatically with a 5 s backoff after the broker drops the connection.
constraints: Subscribe in the MQTT_EVENT_CONNECTED branch of the event handler
Parse payload with strncmp (on / off)
GPIO 2 output, default off
Reconnect handled via MQTT_EVENT_DISCONNECTED plus a 5 s delayed reconnect, not a busy loop
expected: main.c with MQTT command subscription controlling GPIO 2
evaluation: Check GPIO control driven from the MQTT data event

scenario: mqtt qos1 sensor upload with last will
prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that reads the on-chip temperature sensor placeholder value (a static integer that increments), and publishes it as topic device/temp with QoS 1 every 30 s. Configure a last-will message offline on topic device/status.
constraints: QoS 1 on both subscription-relevant publish and last will
Last will topic device/status with payload offline
Publish period 30 s
ESP_ERROR_CHECK on all esp_err_t calls
expected: main.c with MQTT client config including last will and periodic publish
evaluation: Check lwt_timeout/last-will fields set in esp_mqtt_client_config_t
Check qos field set to 1 on publish

scenario: tcp echo server on lwip socket
prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that joins WiFi in station mode and runs a TCP echo server on port 3333 using lwIP sockets: listen, accept one client at a time, echo received bytes back until the peer closes, then accept the next client.
constraints: Use lwIP socket API (socket/bind/listen/accept/recv/send)
Port 3333, backlog at least 1
Close client socket on recv() == 0
recv buffer 512 bytes, loop until connection closed
expected: main.c with WiFi station init and TCP echo server loop
evaluation: Check echo loop using recv and send

prompt: Implement pico-sdk firmware for the Pico W that connects to the local WiFi via CYW43, then as a TCP client connects to server 192.168.1.50:9000 and sends the string PICO-ALIVE every 5 s. If the connection fails, retry after 5 s without crashing.
constraints: Use cyw43_arch_init and cyw43_arch_enable_station_mode with hardcoded SSID/password placeholders
Use lwIP socket or altcp API for the TCP client
Send period 5 s; on send failure close, wait 5 s, reconnect
All network calls must not busy-wait without timeout
expected: main.c with CYW43 station init and TCP client loop
evaluation: Check periodic send with reconnect path

prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that joins WiFi in station mode and broadcasts a UDP datagram HELLO from device <MAC> to 255.255.255.255:4445 every 2 seconds using the lwIP socket API.
constraints: UDP datagram socket (SOCK_DGRAM)
Broadcast destination 255.255.255.255:4445 with SO_BROADCAST enabled
Send every 2 s
Include the device MAC string in the payload
expected: main.c with WiFi init and UDP broadcast loop
evaluation: Check 2 s send loop to port 4445

prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that joins WiFi, then every 60 s performs an HTTP GET to http://192.168.1.20/data using the esp_http_client API, reads up to 256 bytes of the body, logs the first line, and always closes the client. Abort with an error log if the response takes longer than 5 s.
constraints: Use esp_http_client (init / perform / read / cleanup)
Request every 60 s
5 s timeout on the request
ESP_ERROR_CHECK on setup calls; graceful log on timeout
expected: main.c with WiFi init and periodic HTTP GET
evaluation: Check esp_http_client_init with the URL and esp_http_client_cleanup

scenario: ble gatt server with custom service
prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware using NimBLE that starts a BLE GATT server with one custom 128-bit UUID service exposing one readable, writable characteristic. On write, log the received bytes; on read, return a static counter. Advertise with device name ESP-NET-DEV.
constraints: Use NimBLE stack (nimble_port_init, ble_gatts_count_cfg / register, ble_advertising)
One service with one RW characteristic
Device name ESP-NET-DEV in the advertisement
Handle write and access callbacks
expected: main.c with NimBLE host task, GATT service registration and advertising

prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware using NimBLE that continuously scans for BLE advertisements for 3 s windows separated by 2 s idle, and logs each discovered device address and RSSI.
constraints: Use NimBLE gap event BLE_GAP_EVENT_DISC to collect results
3 s scan / 2 s idle duty cycle
Log address and RSSI per device
Do not connect to discovered devices
evaluation: Check RSSI logging in the discovery event

scenario: lora sx1278 spi driver with ocp limit
prompt: Implement STM32 HAL firmware that drives an SX1278 LoRa module over SPI1 (PA5/PA6/PA7, NSS on PA4, DIO0 interrupt on PB0) at 433 MHz: initialise in LoRa mode, send the string LORA-PING every 10 s, and on DIO0 RX-complete interrupt toggle PD12.
constraints: SPI1 master at max 8 MHz, mode 0
SX1278 reset sequence and mode set to LORA via RegOpMode
Frequency 433 MHz written to FrfMSB/Mid/LSB
DIO0 mapped to RX done, handled in EXTI interrupt with HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback
expected: main.c plus sx1278 driver functions over SPI1
evaluation: Check SPI1 init and NSS handling
Check RegOpMode/Frf registers written and EXTI callback present

prompt: Implement ESP-IDF firmware that joins WiFi, starts the SNTP service against pool.ntp.org, and every minute logs the local time obtained from the SNTP-synchronised system time. Synchronisation must wait up to 15 s for a first valid time before logging an error.
constraints: Use esp_netif_sntp or esp_sntp API with pool.ntp.org
Wait up to 15 s for time synchronisation, then log a timeout error
Log time every 60 s using time()/localtime_r
expected: main.c with WiFi init, SNTP start and periodic time logging
evaluation: Check sntp_setserver or config with pool.ntp.org
Check 15 s sync wait and 60 s logging loop

scenario: at modem udp send with response parsing
prompt: Implement STM32 HAL firmware that talks to a BC26/BC95 NB-IoT modem over USART2 (115200 8N1): send AT handshake, attach the network with AT+CGATT=1, then every 60 s open a UDP socket to 120.24.60.20:5683 and send 4 bytes 0x01 0x02 0x03 0x04 using AT+QISEND. Parse modem responses line by line with a 3 s timeout per command and retry once on timeout.
constraints: USART2 interrupt-driven RX into a 256-byte ring buffer
Per-command 3 s timeout, single retry
Check OK / ERROR token after each AT command
Do not block interrupts; keep the ISR minimal
expected: main.c plus an at_send/at_expect helper over USART2
evaluation: Check USART2 init at 115200 and IRQ-based reception
Check CGATT and QISEND command flow with timeout
